tip: German builds the passive with werden plus a past participle, and that participle goes last: 'wird sofort bezahlt'.
For a passive in the past, use wurde, the past of werden: 'Das Paket wurde geliefert'.
In the passive, von plus dative names the doer: 'von der Polizei' says who did the catching.
Verbs ending in -ieren form the participle without ge-: reparieren gives 'repariert', not gerepariert.
Separable verbs put ge- between the prefix and the stem: aufräumen becomes 'aufgeräumt'.
A modal with the passive ends in a past participle plus werden: 'darf ... genommen werden'.
Reported speech uses Konjunktiv I: 'sei' instead of ist signals you are relaying what someone else said.
sein has an irregular Sie-command: it is 'Seien Sie', never 'Sind Sie'.
The du-command of sein is simply 'Sei', with no ending: 'Sei ehrlich'.
In a command a separable prefix moves to the end: anrufen gives 'Ruf mich an'.
Strong verbs with e shift to i in the du-command: essen becomes 'Iss'.
The ihr-command copies the present ihr-form without 'ihr': 'Setzt euch ... hin'.
With separable verbs, zu slots inside the word: ausschalten becomes 'auszuschalten'.
empfehlen puts the person in the dative and the thing in the accusative: 'uns ein hervorragendes Restaurant'.
warten pairs with auf plus the accusative to mean wait for: 'Warte auf mich'.
A plural adjective with no article takes the ending -e: 'rote Rosen'.
vorhaben (to plan) is separable, so vor- splits to the end: 'ich habe vor, ...'.
German uses no article for having an illness: 'Fieber hat', not 'ein Fieber hat'.
A nachdem clause takes the perfect tense for the earlier action: 'nachdem der Chef eingetroffen ist'.
Motion verbs like fahren form the perfect with sein, not haben: 'er gefahren ist'.
während takes the genitive: 'während des Urlaubs', not 'dem Urlaub'.
When a sentence opens with a non-subject, the verb stays second and the subject follows: 'Statt des Autos nehmen wir'.
After ein, a neuter adjective takes -es: 'ein dickes Buch'.
Add -er to an adjective to compare: leise becomes 'leiser', quieter.
